items.title: Ed Polcer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: The intensity of certain players, Muggsy Spanier and the beautiful intensity of Ruby Braff. Those are probably the strongest influences on me.

ctx.x: I mean the shake or the wobble that I have as a part of my style was really out of Louis, I mean from listening out of Louis and from listening to Louis. And the melodic part I think the combination of me playing the xylophone and seeing those chords [scats] and listening to Hackett and his weaving notes, so I think that’s part of my playing is that. The intensity of certain players, Muggsy Spanier and the beautiful intensity of Ruby Braff. Those are probably the strongest influences on me. I don’t listen that…
That’s an important statement. I like my style you said.
